_README: ep61's 19 `Speaker ?` blocks: the short interjections no diarizer run could cluster.
The owner asked for these to be attempted. They were NOT named from the sensing score,
because the score is measurably unreliable on exactly this class -- of the 5 the gold
passage covers it got 2 right and 3 wrong, and on the two solid text matches (100% and
88% overlap) it got both wrong, one of them a block whose own text says `si Haziq ni`.
So each was resolved from better evidence, or left alone:
3 from the OWNER'S GOLD -- see data/speaker_from_gold.json. [01:47], [01:55], [02:36],
all Rafizi. The gold outranks everything else here.
11 from VIDEO, listed under ep61_speaker_q_video_confirmed. Every one shows the same
man in the orange bomber jacket with his mouth moving, held across the whole padded
2:25:03. All Rafizi.
5 LEFT AS `Speaker ?`, because the camera cannot answer them:
[02:53] and [21:35] -- a full-screen graphic fills the shot (a TikTok/ChatGPT slide,
and the Tabung Haji / Baitul Maqdis card). No speaker is on screen at all.
[07:44] -- a two-shot, which frames_at.py's docstring is explicit proves nothing.
[14:52] and [15:19] -- the camera CUTS WITHIN the block, bomber jacket to olive tee
and back, so these two blocks each hold both voices. They need splitting, not
naming, and the split point cannot be placed from a 9-second block with one
timestamp. Left for the owner's ear.
PATTERN WORTH KEEPING. On this class the sensing's Rafizi calls held up (12 of 12 where
anything could check them) and its Haziq calls did not (0 of 2). The co-host direction is
where the false positives land on short blocks, which is the opposite of raw.md's
original bias and worth re-testing on the next episode rather than assumed.
